steps.note: Make the app store '' instead of NULL for guest orders. The column is still nullable, so old and new pods can run side by side during the rolling update.
Let terminating old pods finish their in-flight requests (3 s drain + shutdown) so nothing writes NULL any more.

Backfill existing guest orders NULL -> '' in small primary-key ranges, committing after each batch: only short row locks, no long transaction, app traffic unaffected. Single DO statement so the in-block COMMITs are allowed.
steps.sql: DO $$ DECLARE lo bigint; maxid bigint; step constant bigint := 20000; BEGIN SELECT min(id), max(id) INTO lo, maxid FROM orders; WHILE lo <= maxid LOOP UPDATE orders SET email = '' WHERE id >= lo AND id < lo + step AND email IS NULL; COMMIT; lo := lo + step; PERFORM pg_sleep(0.02); END LOOP; END $$;

steps.note: Add CHECK (email IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID: enforced for new rows from now on, no table scan. Needs only a brief ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, taken with a short lock_timeout and retried so app queries never queue behind it for long. Skipped if it already exists.
steps.sql: DO $$ BEGIN FOR i IN 1..60 LOOP BEGIN SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '300ms'; IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint WHERE conrelid = 'public.orders'::regclass AND conname = 'orders_email_not_null') THEN ALTER TABLE public.orders ADD CONSTRAINT orders_email_not_null CHECK (email IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID; END IF; RETURN; EXCEPTION WHEN lock_not_available THEN PERFORM pg_sleep(1); END; END LOOP; RAISE EXCEPTION 'could not lock orders to add the check constraint'; END $$;

steps.note: Safety sweep: convert any NULL that slipped in between the backfill and the constraint (e.g. a straggling old pod). Normally updates 0 rows; takes only a ROW EXCLUSIVE lock.
steps.sql: UPDATE public.orders SET email = '' WHERE email IS NULL;

steps.note: Validate the constraint: full scan under SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE, which does not block reads or inserts.
steps.sql: ALTER TABLE public.orders VALIDATE CONSTRAINT orders_email_not_null;

steps.note: SET NOT NULL (Postgres skips the table scan because the valid CHECK proves no NULLs), then drop the now-redundant CHECK. Both in one short transaction with a short lock_timeout and retries.
steps.sql: DO $$ BEGIN FOR i IN 1..60 LOOP BEGIN SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '300ms'; ALTER TABLE public.orders ALTER COLUMN email SET NOT NULL; ALTER TABLE public.orders DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS orders_email_not_null; RETURN; EXCEPTION WHEN lock_not_available THEN PERFORM pg_sleep(1); END; END LOOP; RAISE EXCEPTION 'could not lock orders to set NOT NULL'; END $$;
